channel.title: Daily Recap — 🚀 Space News
channel.description: What happened in 🚀 Space News, recapped daily from subscribed feeds.

item.title: SpaceX launches final set of ISS roll-out solar arrays on CRS-35
item.description:
Under a sunrise glow on Tuesday, a SpaceX Falcon 9 lifted off from pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 6:33 a.m. EDT, carrying the CRS-35 cargo mission to the International Space Station. The first-stage booster (B1096) completed its eighth trip to space, landing back at Landing Zone 40 less than eight minutes after liftoff, while Cargo Dragon C211 separated for a two-day journey to the station.

The Dragon is hauling more than 6,300 pounds of science and supplies, headlined by the fourth and final pair of Roll-Out Solar Arrays (ROSA) built by Redwire Space. Each array provides more than 20 kW of power for over a decade, and their installation completes a multi-year ISS power upgrade that began with a 2017 tech demo. The manifest also supports over 40 scientific studies, including experiments on unconventional glass made from heavier elements that could yield optics tougher than diamond and hardware for lunar rovers. Dragon is expected to dock at the Harmony module's space-facing port Thursday morning and stay about a month.

Sources

  • Spaceflight Now: SpaceX launches NASA science and cargo to the International Space Station

item.title: Perseverance surpasses Opportunity's Mars driving record
item.description:
On sol 2,006 (Oct. 11), Perseverance's 299.6-foot drive pushed its total Martian distance beyond the 28.06 miles (45.16 km) logged by Opportunity over its 15-year mission, making it the longest-driven rover in Red Planet history. NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory marked the feat with a photo journal image of the navcam's view over rover tracks on a rocky slope, an infographic comparing off-world rover driving distances across the Moon and Mars, and a team photo in the Mars Yard with a Guinness World Records certificate.

The record matters because it reflects how far the mission has pushed beyond its original two-year prime mission: Perseverance and Curiosity are both still operating and moving, with the team using its twin rover OPTIMISM to plan drives. After more than five years on Mars, the rover keeps racking up distance as it hunts signs of ancient life in Jezero Crater.

Sources

  • NASA: Perseverance Navcam Image Marks Record Drive
  • NASA: NASA's Record-Setting Perseverance Rover Team
  • NASA: Comparing Off-World Rover Driving Distances

item.title: Griffin-1 lunar lander clears environmental testing at JPL
item.description:
Voyager Technologies' Griffin-1 lunar lander completed nearly three months of environmental testing at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in late September, clearing a major milestone on its path to the Moon. The tests subjected the spacecraft to the harsh conditions of launch, its transit to the Moon, and landing on the surface, demonstrating that it is prepared for the full mission profile.

Griffin-1 is one of the private-sector landers aiming to deliver cargo to the lunar surface under NASA's commercial lunar partnerships, and finishing the final trial at JPL puts the vehicle in line for a future launch opportunity. Voyager released a photo journal documenting the lander after its trials.

Sources

  • NASA: Voyager Technologies' Griffin-1 Completes Environmental Testing at NASA JPL

item.title: NASA names astronaut Christina Koch acting deputy chief engineer
item.description:
NASA announced that astronaut and engineer Christina Koch will serve as the agency's acting deputy chief engineer beginning Sunday, Nov. 1, following the retirement of Katherine Van Hooser, who concludes more than 35 years of service on Oct. 21. In the role, Koch will help lead NASA's engineering community across its centers and missions.

The appointment brings a high-profile flight veteran into a top technical leadership post: Koch is best known for her long-duration missions to the International Space Station, and her engineering background spans electrical engineering and NASA flight-system development. It's a notable example of NASA putting experienced astronaut-engineers into institutional engineering governance at a time when the agency's lunar and Mars programs demand tight technical oversight.

Sources

  • NASA: NASA Names Astronaut Christina Koch Acting Deputy Chief Engineer

item.title: SpaceX to launch solar arrays and 6,300 pounds of cargo to the ISS
item.description:
NASA and SpaceX are set to launch new solar arrays and 6,300 pounds of cargo to the International Space Station aboard the CRS-35 mission, lifting off Tuesday at 6:33 a.m. EDT from Cape Canaveral. The research manifest focuses on human and plant health plus drug-resistant organisms — the kind of applied science the station does best.

It's a fitting capstone to a busy day for SpaceX, which also launched 27 Starlink satellites from California on Monday evening.

  • NASA: NASA’s SpaceX CRS-35 Mission to Launch Health Research

item.title: Antarctic sea ice reaches third-lowest maximum on record
item.description:
Antarctic sea ice grew to its 2026 maximum — and it's the third-lowest maximum extent since satellite observations began. The southern ice story remains the concerning one: the Arctic gets the headlines, but Antarctica's shrinking winter maximums are the trend to watch.

Sources

  • NASA: Antarctic Sea Ice Grows to Its 2026 Maximum

item.title: APOD: ice fishing for cosmic neutrinos
item.description:
Today's Astronomy Picture of the Day goes to the South Pole — 'ice fishing' for cosmic neutrinos with detectors buried in Antarctic ice.

A beautiful reminder that some of the universe's most elusive particles are caught not with telescopes, but with a cubic kilometer of ice and a lot of patience.

Sources

  • NASA: APOD: 2026 October 11 – Ice Fishing for Cosmic Neutrinos

item.title: NASA flyover and fan events at MetLife Stadium
item.description:
NASA announced a flyover plus fan-engagement events at MetLife Stadium, bringing the space agency's outreach directly to an NFL audience.

It's part of a broader, ongoing push to meet the public where they already are rather than expecting them to come to NASA. Sports tie-ins have become one of the agency's favorite outreach channels.

Sources

  • NASA: NASA to Conduct Flyover, Engage NFL Fans at MetLife Stadium

item.title: Astronomy Picture of the Day: the lunar farside
item.description:
Today's Astronomy Picture of the Day showcases the lunar farside — the hemisphere of the Moon permanently turned away from Earth — in striking detail.

It's a reminder of how much of our nearest neighbor we never see from the ground, and why farside missions remain scientifically compelling.

Sources
